text: A woman on metformin developed lactic acidosis. The event was attributed to the drug.
The patient took omeprazole for reflux. She later had hypomagnesaemia, a relationship with the drug could not be excluded.
Olanzapine was started in March. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome occurred and resolved after the drug was stopped.
He had myositis. This was unrelated to atorvastatin and was due to a viral illness.
Atorvastatin was prescribed. Myositis was not considered related to the medication.
Clopidogrel was given after stenting. Bleeding was noted at the access site.
The doctor suspected that paracetamol overdose caused hepatic failure.
Hepatic failure was possibly linked to acetaminophen.
Metformin was continued. No lactic acidosis was observed.
Following omeprazole, the patient experienced nausea. Nausea abated on dechallenge.
Olanzapine and metformin were co-prescribed. Lactic acidosis was attributed to metformin.
